route: Czechia has no dedicated independent-means permit. Non-EU people who are not working or studying use a long-term visa or long-term residence permit for another purpose, with proof of funds. Whatever the purpose, Act 326/1999 requires 'doklad o cestovnim zdravotnim pojisteni, ktere odpovida podminkam uvedenym v par. 180j'. Par. 180j(1): 'Vyse sjednaneho limitu pojistneho plneni na jednu pojistnou udalost cini nejmene 400 000 EUR, a to bez spolucasti pojisteneho'. Par. 180j(5): a foreigner who arrives on a travel-type policy must 'nejpozdeji do 90 dnu ode dne vstupu na uzemi Ceske republiky uzavrit cestovni zdravotni pojisteni v rozsahu komplexni zdravotni pece podle odstavce 8', and the policy must be taken out with an insurer licensed in Czechia where the application is made in the country (par. 180j(6)). Comprehensive care means (par. 180j(8)) care by the insurer's contracted providers 'bez prime uhrady nakladu na leceni pojistenym', with no exclusion of preventive care.
policy: Pojistovna VZP (pVZP) 'Komplexni zdravotni pojisteni cizincu' (the Plus and Exclusive products have a 10 million CZK limit per event; the cheaper 'Zakladni' product has 1.8 million CZK at the low end and may not meet the EUR 400,000 rule). pVZP says its product is 'Akceptovano Odborem azylove a migracni politiky (OAMP)'. Price used: a broker's reprint of the pVZP price table, 12 months, age band 45-59: CZK 19,500 per person a year. Product tier and effective date are not stated by the broker. Slavia and UNIQA comprehensive cover is suspended or not priced (broker says UNIQA comprehensive sales were suspended on 2 Aug 2021).
working: 2 people x CZK 19,500 a year = CZK 39,000 a year; 39,000 / 12 = CZK 3,250 a month.

typical_private.description: Same pVZP comprehensive policy as the main figure; no separate 'typical' premium was found.

eu_citizen_difference: EU/EEA citizens are exempt from the par. 180j policy (par. 180j(4) and the registration regime for Union citizens) and use the public system, or an S1/EHIC, on arrival. Not detailed here.
spot_check: Older broker pricelist (same product line, about 2017-2019): CZK 12,860 per person per year at 45-59, so CZK 2,143 a month for two, against CZK 3,250 now. The two do not agree because they are years apart and the newer table's product tier is unknown. Official premium not reached.
uncertainty: The figure is a broker's reprint, not an insurer or regulator source, and could be for a lower-limit product than the EUR 400,000 rule needs (pVZP 'Plus' and 'Exclusive' have a CZK 10 million limit, about EUR 400,000 at roughly CZK 25/EUR). The real premium could be higher. Dental, outpatient cost-sharing and exclusions were not read. After permanent residence (normally 5 years) the couple would enter the public system; the VZP page then gives CZK 3,024 per person a month for a person with no taxable income (CZK 6,048 a month for two). The rule that only permanent residents (or employees) join the public system comes from general knowledge of Act 48/1997 and was not checked in this session. Income from the ETF would not change that fixed charge, but the tax agent should confirm whether capital income counts.

statutory_must_pay.what: Nothing fixed: public insurance (VZP) is not open to a non-working non-EU couple on a long-term residence permit; they must hold commercial cover until permanent residence (see the file's `route`).

private_plan.terms: In- and out-patient comprehensive cover for foreigners, accepted by the immigration office; limit CZK 10 million per event on the Plus and Exclusive tiers. Deductible and co-payments not read.
private_plan.pricing: Same figure as the file's `amount`: broker reprint of the pVZP table, age band 45-59, CZK 19,500 per person a year; 2 x 19,500 / 12 = CZK 3,250 a month. Product tier and date are not stated by the broker. A search excerpt of Charles University's Slavia price list (2025) shows about CZK 1,200 a month for a basic foreigners' policy, so this is mid-range rather than basic.
